purpose: T060's demanded registration: does e108's two-cluster V-cos step (0.403 self vs 0.141/0.138 any differently-trained net) reduce to a LOW-DIM principal subspace of the recipient's own V-manifold — a self-signature — or is identity the whole 32-d manifold? Recipient own-run anchor-band V (324 splice positions x 8 rows x 16 (layer,head) groups x 32-d, e099's V representation) PCA'd per group (uncentered second moment); each donor's spliced V-set (sibling=e099 randomize / middle=e108 e040_ref / foreign=e105 e021_task, regenerated bit-exactly per the rigs' determinism pins) projected onto the top-k subspace: energy fraction vs k + cos-in-subspace vs k + same-norm gaussian nulls. FROZEN bars: sibling>=2x foreign at k<=8 with null below both => LOW-DIM SELF-SIGNATURE (name k); 2x never fires in k=1..31 => HIGH-DIM IDENTITY.

seeds.note: every stream is a published seed; NO new sampling

protocol.band: positions 64..387 (324), the e099/e105/e108 splice targets (events g=100..420 K=32, age>96, replaced once at first admission)
protocol.v_representation: per-(layer,head) 32-d V vectors at (row, position); 16 groups x 2592 vectors = 41,472 per set — the exact population the e099 repl_stats instrument scores
protocol.pca: uncentered second-moment eigendecomposition per group (mean direction included; mean-mode share reported)
protocol.energy_fraction: projected energy / total energy in the top-k axes, pooled over the 16 groups (norm-weighted)
protocol.cos_in_subspace: mean|cos_k(old, donor)| between top-k projections of the captured splice-time pairs; k=32 == the published e108 V-cos
protocol.null: R=64 same-norm gaussian-direction replicates per donor set; analytic reference k/32

gates.threads_note: e080 module import sets 12; overridden to 8 (task spec / T050)

G4b_verbatim_bit_identity.rule: capture skeletons bit-identical to e080.generate_arm / e099.generate_arm5 (fresh seed-7 streams)

G4a_published_match.note: four arms vs runs/e108/metrics.json: tail tokens + repl_stats floats, max dev 0.00e+00 (bar 1e-12)

cos_in_subspace.note: k=1 is degenerate: two 1-d projections are collinear, so |cos_1| = 1 for EVERY arm — the instrument is informative from k=2; k=32 == the published e108 V-cos exactly

frozen_rules.low_dim: EXISTS k <= 8: E_sibling(k) >= 2.0x E_foreign(k) AND null97(k) < both => LOW-DIM SELF-SIGNATURE (name k*)
frozen_rules.high_dim: 2x separation at NO k in 1..31 => HIGH-DIM IDENTITY
frozen_rules.else_: INTERMEDIATE (first firing k in 9..31; name it)

null_below_both.rule: null97(k) < min(sibling, foreign) E(k) for k <= 8

low_dim.rule: EXISTS k <= 8: ratio >= 2.0x AND null below both

high_dim.rule: the 2x separation itself fires at NO k in 1..31 (k=32 trivial: all curves -> 1)

cos_separation_k.rule: smallest k whose self-arm mean|cos_k| row-bootstrap CI clears both other arms' CIs (holding through k=32)

registered_decision.verdict: LOW-DIM SELF-SIGNATURE fires: the sibling donor's spliced V-set carries >= 2x the foreign donor's energy in the recipient's top-7 principal subspace (sibling 0.815 vs foreign 0.220 = 3.71x at k=7; same-norm null 0.219, below both) — the anchor's identity check is a k=7-dim readout of the V-manifold. The 0.40/0.14 step reduces to a low-dimensional self-signature. HONEST CAVEATS: (1) the 2x clause holds at EVERY k<=8 (11.7x at k=1, 3.4x at k=8) — k*=7 is set by the null clause, which clears only at k=7 and only at the 98th percentile of the null (margin 0.0003); at k<=5 and k=8 the foreign/middle donors sit AT or BELOW the isotropic null (0th percentile). The sharper reading is EXCLUSION, not graded alignment: the sibling occupies the recipient's principal structure at the null's 100th percentile at every k (E(8) 0.841 vs own in-sample 0.837 vs null 0.250), while differently-trained nets' V-manifolds carry ZERO excess over chance — the self-signature is exclusive. (2) The pairwise-cos variant separates self from other already at k=2 (k=1 |cos| is trivially 1 for every arm).
